A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CR-CTC study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASR experiments on LibriSpeech, Aishell-1, and GigaSpeech, including component ablations, decoding comparisons, and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds an EMA-teacher comparison, beam-size experiments, and results using a Conformer encoder.

M1.justification: The proposed CR-CTC and SR-CTC procedures remain unchanged, including their losses and augmentation strategy. The x-to-z loss notation and depth-wise convolution description clarify existing operations. EMA-distilled CTC is introduced as a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same English and Mandarin ASR tasks on LibriSpeech, Aishell-1, and GigaSpeech. The additional encoder and decoding experiments use existing LibriSpeech coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds EMA-distilled CTC to the self-distillation comparison in Table 4. Existing comparator membership in Tables 1–3 and 7 is retained; the new Conformer experiment uses the already evaluated CTC, CTC/AED, and pruned-transducer families.

E3.justification: v3 adds prefix-search experiments with beam sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8, plus a 12-layer Conformer evaluation with specified architecture and training budgets (Appendices A.3 and A.7). Previously reported evaluation settings remain unchanged; additional decoding descriptions clarify existing experiments.

E4.justification: Targeted additions test an EMA teacher as an alternative self-distillation approach, sensitivity to decoding beam width, and transfer of the gains to a Conformer encoder (Tables 4, 14, and 17). Existing masking, peak-suppression, auxiliary-head, and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for the experimental results. v3 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged. v3 adds EMA-distilled CTC at 2.31/5.25% WER (Table 4), identical scores across the tested beam widths (Table 14), and Conformer results (Table 17): CR-CTC achieves 2.43/5.78%, versus 2.92/7.15% for CTC, 2.50/5.94% for CTC/AED, and 2.49/5.87% for pruned transducer, on test-clean/test-other.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.6 formally defines the EMA-teacher update, its step-dependent decay, and the distillation and total losses in Equations 7–8. Existing mathematical formulations are unchanged apart from equivalent loss-input notation; no proofs or theoretical guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The central performance-parity and three-mechanism contributions are retained. v3 adds an explicit priority claim in Section 2 that it is the first approach to bring pure CTC to transducer and CTC/AED performance, strengthening the stated novelty without changing the principal contribution.

C2.justification: v3 newly argues that supervision from the main CTC loss avoids training problems associated with unsupervised consistency objectives. It also interprets the EMA comparison as evidence of superior self-distillation and the Conformer results as support for generalization across encoders. The original three mechanism explanations remain intact.

D1.justification: v3 documents Zipformer stack frame rates, transducer beam size and inference-head choices, SR-CTC's depth-wise convolution, and implementation settings for the new EMA and Conformer experiments. It also explicitly announces code release at the icefall address already cited in v1; the PDFs do not establish when access changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands the positioning against image consistency learning, self/semi-supervised ASR, and supervised CTC methods. It adds discussion of MoCo, Speech SimCLR, C-Siam, and shortcut learning, clarifies distinctions from Gao et al. and Cons-KD, and introduces explicit priority claims. This exceeds a limited citation update.

P1.justification: The abstract and consistency-regularization discussion are revised, notation and explanatory passages are clarified, and Appendices A.6–A.7 are added. The overall section organization and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives revised arrows and loss labels, Table 4 gains an EMA row, and new Tables 14 and 17 present beam-width and Conformer results. Existing tables are repositioned closer to their discussion, while Figure 2 and the main display conventions are retained.

improvement.justification: The EMA comparison, beam-width study, and Conformer evaluation strengthen validation, especially by showing that the reported benefit extends beyond Zipformer. Added implementation details and clearer distinctions from prior work improve reproducibility and interpretation. These gains are incremental: the main results remain unchanged, and the new comparisons still lack uncertainty estimates.
